paragraphs.title: The Concubine Leaves and the Levite Goes to Bring Her Back

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that a certain Levite was sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim.
easy.q: Who was sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim?

answers: To her father's house in Bethlehemjudah
easy.explanation: She went away from the Levite unto her father's house in Bethlehemjudah.
Her husband arose and went after her to speak friendly unto her and bring her again.

answers: To speak friendly unto her and bring her again
medium.explanation: The text states that he went after her to speak friendly unto her and bring her again.
medium.q: Why did the Levite go after the concubine?

medium.explanation: Verse 2 says she was there four whole months.
medium.q: How long was the concubine at her father's house?

answers: There was no king in Israel
Israel was at war with Egypt
medium.explanation: The chapter begins, “when there was no king in Israel.”
medium.q: What circumstance is mentioned at the beginning of the story?

answers: He was traveling on a journey
He was working in a field
challenge.explanation: The servant and two donkeys accompanied him as he traveled to Bethlehemjudah.
challenge.q: What does the servant and the couple of asses suggest about the Levite's journey?

challenge.explanation: The concubine was from Bethlehemjudah, while the Levite sojourned near mount Ephraim.
challenge.q: Which locations are contrasted in these verses?

answers: Speak friendly unto her and bring her again
challenge.explanation: His stated purpose was to speak friendly unto her and bring her again.
challenge.q: What did the Levite intend to do when he reached the concubine?

paragraphs.title: Hospitality at the Father’s House and the Delayed Departure

easy.explanation: When the girl's father saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
easy.q: Who rejoiced to meet the Levite?

easy.explanation: He abode with the father three days.
easy.q: How many days did the Levite initially remain at the house?

easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly describe them eating and drinking together.
easy.q: What did the Levite and his host do during the hospitality?

answers: He urged the Levite to eat and remain
medium.explanation: He urged him to comfort his heart, tarry, and eat before departing.
medium.q: How did the girl's father delay the departure?

answers: Called to him from far away
medium.explanation: The father persuaded the Levite to lodge there again.
medium.q: What does “urged him” mean in this context?

answers: The father asked them to eat and tarry until afternoon
medium.explanation: The father told him to comfort his heart, and they tarried until afternoon.
medium.q: Why was the departure delayed on the fifth day?

answers: The stay extended from three days into further delays on the fourth and fifth days
challenge.explanation: After three days, the father persuaded the Levite to remain again on the fourth and fifth days.
challenge.q: What change occurred during the hospitality?

answers: The day drew toward evening before they left
challenge.explanation: The father said that the day was drawing toward evening and growing to an end.
challenge.q: What was the result of the repeated delays?

challenge.explanation: The Levite rose to depart with his concubine and his servant.
challenge.q: Who finally departed with the Levite?

paragraphs.title: Refusing to Stay in Jebus and Reaching Gibeah

easy.explanation: He came over against Jebus but would not tarry there that night.
easy.q: In which city did the Levite refuse to lodge?

easy.explanation: The Levite said, “We will pass over to Gibeah.”
easy.q: To which city did they decide to continue?

answers: No man took them into his house
easy.explanation: They sat in a street because there was no man that took them into his house.
easy.q: What happened when they arrived in Gibeah?

answers: It was a city of strangers and not of the children of Israel
medium.explanation: He said they would not turn into a city that was not of the children of Israel.
medium.q: Why did the Levite refuse to lodge in Jebus?

answers: They entered a house in Jebus
They left Jebus in the morning
medium.explanation: The phrase describes their location near Jebus as the day was far spent.
medium.q: What does “when they were by Jebus” indicate?

answers: They wanted to eat in Bethlehemjudah
medium.explanation: The servant noted that the day was far spent and suggested lodging in the city.
medium.q: Why did they need to find another place before night?

answers: The approaching night and the continuation of their journey
A desire to return to Bethlehemjudah
challenge.explanation: As the day ended, they continued to Gibeah to find lodging.
challenge.q: What caused them to seek lodging in Gibeah?

answers: No one had yet taken them into a house
They preferred not to enter a house
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says there was no man that took them into his house.
challenge.q: What can be understood from their sitting in the street?

answers: An old man coming from his work out of the field
A young man of the city
challenge.explanation: An old man from mount Ephraim came from the field at evening and saw the wayfaring man.

paragraphs.title: The Old Man Welcomes the Travelers

answers: A man of mount Ephraim who sojourned in Gibeah
One of the sons of Belial
easy.explanation: The old man was also of mount Ephraim and sojourned in Gibeah.

answers: Whither he was going and whence he came
easy.explanation: He asked, “Whither goest thou? and whence comest thou?”
easy.q: What did the old man ask the traveler?

answers: A house, food, and care for the donkeys
easy.explanation: He brought them into his house, gave provender to the donkeys, and provided food and drink.
easy.q: What did the old man provide for the travelers?

answers: He was going to the house of the Lord
medium.explanation: The Levite said, “I am now going to the house of the Lord.”
medium.q: What did the Levite say about his destination?

answers: Takes me into a house for lodging
Drives me out of the city
medium.explanation: The Levite meant that no one had taken him into a house.
medium.q: What does “receiveth me to house” mean?

answers: They had straw, provender, bread, and wine
The old man had already fed them
medium.explanation: He said they had supplies for the donkeys and food and drink for the travelers.
medium.q: Why did the Levite say they had no want?

answers: He did not want him to lodge in the street
He wanted to take the donkeys
He did not understand the traveler
challenge.explanation: The old man said, “only lodge not in the street,” and brought him into his house.
challenge.q: Why did the old man still invite the traveler inside?

answers: Bringing them into the house, feeding the donkeys, washing their feet, and eating and drinking
Eating, going to the field, and sleeping in the street
Washing the donkeys, fighting, and feasting
challenge.explanation: These actions occur in that order in verses 20–21.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the old man's hospitality?

answers: The old man welcomed them although no one else had received them
The old man refused to open his house
The old man left before they arrived
challenge.explanation: No one had taken them in, but the old man brought them into his house and cared for them.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the old man and the rest of the city?

paragraphs.title: The Men of the City Attack the House

easy.explanation: Certain sons of Belial from the city beset the house round about.

answers: That the man who entered the house be brought out
That food be given to them
That the city gate be opened
easy.explanation: They said, “Bring forth the man that came into thine house.”

answers: The old master of the house
easy.explanation: The master of the house went out and pleaded with the men not to act wickedly.
easy.q: Who tried to protect the guest?

answers: They surrounded the house and beat at the door
They invited the travelers to a feast
medium.explanation: They beset the house round about and beat at the door.
medium.q: How did the men of the city begin the attack?

medium.explanation: Their violent and immoral conduct identifies them as wicked men.
medium.q: What does “sons of Belial” indicate in this context?

answers: His daughter and the guest's concubine
medium.explanation: He offered to bring out his daughter and the concubine.
medium.q: What did the master of the house offer instead of the male guest?

answers: Act so wickedly and do this folly
Take the guest to another city
challenge.explanation: He pleaded, “do not so wickedly” and “do not this folly.”
challenge.q: What did the master of the house ask the men not to do?

answers: The men would not hearken to him
The old man shut the door and everything ended
challenge.explanation: The text says that the men would not listen to the master of the house.
challenge.q: What shows that the threats did not end immediately?

answers: They demanded the guest, refused to listen, and the concubine was brought out
They requested food and received it
They left after a brief conversation
challenge.explanation: The men demanded the guest, rejected the old man's plea, and the concubine was brought out and abused.
challenge.q: How did the event proceed from the initial demand to the abuse?

paragraphs.title: The Concubine’s Death and the Shock Across Israel

answers: At the door of the house
easy.explanation: She fell down at the door of the man's house where her lord was.
easy.q: Where was the concubine found in the morning?

answers: He placed her upon an ass and went to his place
He returned her to her father
He called the men of the city
easy.explanation: He took her up upon an ass and went to his place.
easy.q: What did the Levite do with her body?

easy.explanation: He divided her into twelve pieces.
easy.q: Into how many pieces did the Levite divide her?

answers: She returned wounded and dying, and then died
She returned safely to her father
medium.explanation: She fell at the door and was later divided into pieces, showing that she had died.
medium.q: What happened to the concubine after the night?

medium.explanation: The Levite divided her body into twelve parts.
medium.q: What does “pieces” mean in the description of the body?

answers: Throughout all the coasts of Israel
Only to the men of Gibeah
medium.explanation: The text says he sent them into all the coasts of Israel.

answers: To call Israel to consider the deed, take advice, and speak their minds
To invite the tribes to a feast
challenge.explanation: The final verse calls the people to consider the deed, take advice, and speak their minds.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of sending the pieces throughout Israel?

challenge.explanation: They said there had been no such deed done or seen from the time Israel came out of Egypt.
challenge.q: What reaction is described among those who saw the deed?

answers: The absence of a king is followed by a call for Israel to deliberate about the deed
The story returns only to Bethlehemjudah
challenge.explanation: The chapter opens by noting that there was no king in Israel and ends with a call to consider and deliberate over the deed.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the opening circumstance?
